Confidence intervals for
multiple correlation coefficients
(R-squared and adjusted R-squared)
are generated using
the `RSqMC()` function from the `betaMC` package.
In this example,
we use the data set and the model used in
[betaMC: Example Using the BetaMC Function](example-beta-mc.html).


``` r
library(package = betaMC)
```




``` r
df <- betaMC::nas1982
```

### Regression

Fit the regression model using the `lm()` function.


``` r
object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)
```

### Monte Carlo Sampling Distribution of Parameters

#### Normal-Theory Approach


``` r
mvn <- MC(object = object, type = "mvn")
```

#### Asymptotic distribution-free Approach


``` r
adf <- MC(object = object, type = "adf")
```

#### Heteroskedasticity Consistent Approach (HC3)


``` r
hc3 <- MC(object = object, type = "hc3")
```

### Multiple Correlation Coefficients

#### Normal-Theory Approach


``` r
mvn <- RSqMC(object = mvn)
```

#### Asymptotic distribution-free Approach


``` r
adf <- RSqMC(object = adf)
```

#### Heteroskedasticity Consistent Approach (HC3)


``` r
hc3 <- RSqMC(object = hc3)
```

## Methods

### summary

Summary of the results of `RSqMC()`.


``` r
summary(object = mvn)
#> Call:
#> RSqMC(object = mvn)
#> 
#> R-squared and adjusted R-squared
#> type = "mvn"
#>        est     se     R  0.05%   0.5%   2.5%  97.5%  99.5% 99.95%
#> rsq 0.8045 0.0561 20000 0.5067 0.6038 0.6605 0.8809 0.9025 0.9283
#> adj 0.7906 0.0601 20000 0.4715 0.5755 0.6363 0.8724 0.8955 0.9232
summary(object = adf)
#> Call:
#> RSqMC(object = adf)
#> 
#> R-squared and adjusted R-squared
#> type = "adf"
#>        est     se     R  0.05%   0.5%   2.5%  97.5%  99.5% 99.95%
#> rsq 0.8045 0.0547 20000 0.5427 0.6122 0.6661 0.8796 0.9025 0.9212
#> adj 0.7906 0.0586 20000 0.5100 0.5845 0.6423 0.8710 0.8956 0.9156
summary(object = hc3)
#> Call:
#> RSqMC(object = hc3)
#> 
#> R-squared and adjusted R-squared
#> type = "hc3"
#>        est     se     R  0.05% 0.5%   2.5% 97.5%  99.5% 99.95%
#> rsq 0.8045 0.0617 20000 0.4685 0.58 0.6481 0.888 0.9111 0.9382
#> adj 0.7906 0.0662 20000 0.4306 0.55 0.6230 0.880 0.9048 0.9338
```

### coef

Return the vector of estimates.


``` r
stats::coef(object = mvn)
#>       rsq       adj 
#> 0.8045263 0.7905638
stats::coef(object = adf)
#>       rsq       adj 
#> 0.8045263 0.7905638
stats::coef(object = hc3)
#>       rsq       adj 
#> 0.8045263 0.7905638
```

### vcov

Return the sampling covariance matrix.


``` r
stats::vcov(object = mvn)
#>             rsq         adj
#> rsq 0.003146481 0.003371229
#> adj 0.003371229 0.003612031
stats::vcov(object = adf)
#>             rsq         adj
#> rsq 0.002990290 0.003203882
#> adj 0.003203882 0.003432730
stats::vcov(object = hc3)
#>             rsq         adj
#> rsq 0.003812644 0.004084976
#> adj 0.004084976 0.004376760
```

### confint

Return confidence intervals.


``` r
stats::confint(object = mvn, level = 0.95)
#>         2.5 %    97.5 %
#> rsq 0.6605064 0.8808726
#> adj 0.6362568 0.8723635
stats::confint(object = adf, level = 0.95)
#>         2.5 %    97.5 %
#> rsq 0.6661370 0.8796453
#> adj 0.6422896 0.8710486
stats::confint(object = hc3, level = 0.95)
#>         2.5 %    97.5 %
#> rsq 0.6480992 0.8879830
#> adj 0.6229635 0.8799818
```
